subject: Sprightly Labs — Prefetch queue drift impacting inference p95
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@sprightly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprightly Labs — Prefetch queue drift impacting inference p95

Hi Sara / Sprightly ops team,

We wanted to let you know we've observed a degradation affecting hosted inference serving for a subset of Sprightly traffic beginning ~08:50 PDT. Symptoms: elevated p95 generation latency (roughly 2-3x normal) and increased token accounting on requests that trigger prefetch/cache warmups. We identified the root symptom as a prefetch queue depth drift after a codepath change to the prefetch prioritizer.

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Rolled back the prioritizer change for your shard at 09:05 PDT.
- Throttled background prefetch workers for Sprightly to reduce contention.
- Fallback routing enabled for latency-sensitive routes to an alternate capacity pool.

Current status: traffic is routing over fallback and p95 is trending back toward baseline, but you may still see intermittent spikes while the prefix cache stabilizes.

Why this matters: we know Sprightly uses low-latency generation for customer-facing flows, and a sustained p95 elevation can materially affect UX. We're treating this as high priority and keeping your account on active monitoring until metrics fully normalize.

Next steps (what we'll do and when):
1) 09:30 PDT: full validation of rollback and queue metrics.
2) 11:00 PDT: if metrics stable for 60m, we'll progressively reenable prioritizer with conservative limits.
3) By EOD: post-incident note + preliminary attachment with snapshot of queue metrics.

Attachments: prefetched queue snapshot (CSV) — small sample of queue lengths and inflight tokens captured at 09:00 PDT.

If you want us to open a dedicated bridge or loop in your SREs, we can do that immediately. Sorry for the interruption and thanks for the quick signal.

— Laura
Laura Bennett

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the rollback. We did see the spike on our side around 08:55 and that lines up with incoming customer complaints about sluggish responses. Appreciate the fallback routing — can you confirm whether the fallback path preserves our current model pin (v20250429) and content filtering? We need to be sure there's no model swap while the fallback is active.

Also, can you share the CSV snapshot and any logs that show the queue depth trend? We'll correlate with our SDK telemetry.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Sprightly Labs — Prefetch queue drift impacting inference p95

Laura / Sara,

Confirming: fallback routing preserves the pinned model (v20250429) and all policy layers (filtering, logging) remain in place. The fallback pool uses identical model artifacts and same KMS keys; only the serving pool changes.

Sharing the quick snapshot now (attached) and adding a short note on what we saw in the metrics: the prefetch prioritizer started queueing background prefetches aggressively when prefix miss rate spiked; queue length doubled and worker backpressure propagated to the generation fast-path for clients with concurrent low-latency connections. Rolling the change back reduced the prefetch worker concurrency by ~60% and restored headroom.

We're keeping a watch on p95 and will only reintroduce the change with traffic shadowing on a canary with Sprightly traffic excluded until we have feature flags gated by inflight thresholds.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Sprightly Labs — Post-incident summary and next steps (INC-20250521-37)

Hi Sara,

Following up with the post-incident summary and a short list of actionable items. Thank you again for your patience while we stabilized traffic.

Summary: At ~08:50 PDT on 2025-05-21 a recent change to the prefetch prioritizer caused sustained queue growth for a subset of customer shards, which increased p95 generation latency for concurrent low-latency flows. We performed a targeted rollback at 09:05 PDT which restored service; fallback routing mitigated user impact during remediation. Root cause: insufficient throttling in the prioritizer when prefix miss rates rose quickly.

Impact: For Sprightly Labs, customers experienced elevated generation p95 for approximately 15-40 minutes depending on session concurrency. No data leakage or model swaps occurred.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back prioritizer change (09:05 PDT).
- Throttled background prefetch workers and reduced concurrency limits (09:10 PDT).
- Enabled fallback routing for latency critical traffic (09:12 PDT).
- Added an automated alert on prefetch queue depth and inflight tokens (deployed 10:20 PDT).

Planned follow-ups:
1) Engineering will implement conservative per-customer inflight thresholds for prefetch workers (ETA 2025-06-04).
2) We'll add a canary gating flag to the prioritizer rollout so Sprightly traffic can be excluded during tests (ETA 2025-06-11).
3) We'll share the full postmortem once the draft is finalized; link is above.

Attached is the CSV snapshot and an initial draft of the postmortem (PDF). We attached only redacted logs in the draft; full internal logs are available under NDA if you want them for your SRE review.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute recap with our SRE leads to walk through the changes and answer questions. Please let me know a few slots that work for you.

Apologies again for the disruption — we value Sprightly as a priority account and will make sure the mitigations reduce recurrence risk.

Best,
Laura
